name: det_interlacing_indicator
summary: Induction on k. If y(0) < x(b+1) for some b, rows 0 and b + 1 are both all ones, so the determinant and the indicator (x(1) ≤ y(0) fails) vanish. Otherwise only the first entry of column 0 can be 1, and expanding along column 0 reduces to the tails.

steps.lean:
induction' k with k ih
  · simp
  obtain ⟨b, h⟩ | h := exists_or_forall_not fun b ↦ y 0 < x (succ b)
  · rw [det_zero_of_row_eq b.succ_ne_zero] <;> [grind [hy b.castSucc.zero_le]; ext c]
    grind [of_apply, hy c.zero_le, hx b.succ.zero_le]
  simp [det_succ_column_zero', sum_univ_succ, forall_fin_succ, h]
  erw [ih] <;> grind [Antitone]

steps.claim: k = 0: the empty determinant is 1 and the condition is vacuous.
k + 1, with induction hypothesis ih for decreasing sequences of length k: distinguish whether y(0) < x(b+1) for some b.
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨b, h⟩ | h := exists_or_forall_not fun b ↦ y 0 < x (succ b)
  · rw [det_zero_of_row_eq b.succ_ne_zero] <;> [grind [hy b.castSucc.zero_le]; ext c]
    grind [of_apply, hy c.zero_le, hx b.succ.zero_le]
  simp [det_succ_column_zero', sum_univ_succ, forall_fin_succ, h]
  erw [ih] <;> grind [Antitone]

steps.claim: If y(0) < x(b+1) for some b: rows 0 and b + 1 are equal (for every c, y(c) ≤ y(0) < x(b+1) ≤ x(0), so both entries are 1), hence the determinant is 0; and the condition fails, since x(1) ≥ x(b+1) > y(0).
steps.lean:
· rw [det_zero_of_row_eq b.succ_ne_zero] <;> [grind [hy b.castSucc.zero_le]; ext c]
    grind [of_apply, hy c.zero_le, hx b.succ.zero_le]

steps.claim: Otherwise x(b+1) ≤ y(0) for every b: in column 0 only the entry at row 0 can be 1, so expanding along column 0 gives [y(0) < x(0)] times the determinant of the same kind for the tails (x(1..), y(1..)), which ih evaluates; the conditions match.
steps.lean:
simp [det_succ_column_zero', sum_univ_succ, forall_fin_succ, h]
  erw [ih] <;> grind [Antitone]
